- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 2–3 periods.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid underreaction.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses mean reversion; if price deviates >3σ from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast toward mean by 0.5–1.5% per period.  
- When sentiment peaks coincide with price peaks, model often fails to anticipate subsequent drop; delay forecast correction by 1–2 periods after sentiment peak.
